body:
WHAT THE CODE ALREADY DOES FOR EACH ROW, so the walk tests the right thing (read 6 Nov 2026, main e394d03; NOTHING here was run: docs/33 PB-F9, F15 to F18 are still "not verified").

PB-F15 (a call, another app, a navigation voice) and PB-F16 (headphones or Bluetooth unplugged): the app has no handler of its own, on purpose. `JustAudioBackend` creates the player with `handleInterruptions: true` and `androidApplyAudioAttributes: true` (app/lib/playback/just_audio_backend.dart:30-33) and `bootstrap.dart:92-98` configures `AudioSessionConfiguration.music()`. So pause, duck, resume and the "becoming noisy" pause are the library's defaults. Two things the walk must watch, because the engine does not know about them: (1) a pause or resume made by the library arrives only as a backend state change (`_onBackendState`, playback_engine.dart:1210), it never moves `_intent`; a song that waits for its server or its connection (`_waitingSince`) is not started by a focus resume, which is right; (2) after a call, the lock screen and the mini player must agree with the audio (the B-51 family: they copy `isPlaying`). There is no fake of the audio session in the repository, so G-4's "write tests with the audio-session fake" means writing that fake first (`AudioSession.instance.interruptionEventStream`).

PB-F9 (paused for hours, then Play): the signed song address lives 6 hours. The app caches it with its expiry and a margin (data/encore/signed_addresses.dart:39-52, renewed when expired), but the PLAYER holds the old address it was given. By reading, the path is: Play on the old address -> 401 -> `_onBackendError` -> `_judgeFailure` -> the one quiet retry (`_retried`, 1369-1373) -> `_loadCurrent` -> `resolve` -> a new address. That should work; it is not proved. The test is cheap and needs no phone: a fake clock past the expiry in test/playback/playback_engine_test.dart (the `Harness`), a backend that fails once, expect a second `setSources` with a new address and sound.

PB-F17 (full disk) and PB-F18 (damaged download): downloads fail with the raw text in `downloads.last_error` which no screen shows (see the P2-22 note: the phone's reasons must be written in words there). A damaged file is the player's error path, same as PB-25.

HOW TO PROVOKE THEM on the emulator (untested here): a call with `adb emu gsm call 5551234` and `adb emu gsm cancel 5551234`; the "becoming noisy" broadcast needs a rootable emulator image; a full disk with a large file written under `/data/local/tmp` until the free space is below the app's guard (`StorageGuard.defaultMinFreeBytes`). On a real phone: a Bluetooth speaker switched off, a wired headset pulled out.

RECORD each result in docs/33 (the Built/Open column and the test column) and docs/evidence/README.md in the PR, as the walk rules say (docs/07 section 12).
